gloss: to start running; to break into a run

definitions.gloss: to start running; to break into a run
definitions.explanation: To suddenly begin running. Describes the moment when someone transitions from standing or walking into a running motion.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちが{校庭|こうてい}に{走|はし}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: The children broke into a run toward the schoolyard.

examples.japanese: {信号|しんごう}が{青|あお}になったら{走|はし}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: When the light turned green, I started running.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{急|きゅう}に{走|はし}り{出|だ}して{姿|すがた}が{見|み}えなくなった。
examples.english: He suddenly started running and disappeared from sight.

notes:
CONJUGATION:
・{走|はし}り{出|だ}す → {走|はし}り{出|だ}さない (negative)
・{走|はし}り{出|だ}す → {走|はし}り{出|だ}して (te-form)
・{走|はし}り{出|だ}す → {走|はし}り{出|だ}した (past)

FORMATION:
Compound verb: {走|はし}る (to run) + {出|だ}す (to begin)

The ～{出|だ}す pattern indicates the beginning of an action. With motion verbs, it emphasizes the moment of transition into that motion.

SIMILAR COMPOUND VERBS:
・{歩|ある}き{出|だ}す - to start walking
・{泳|およ}ぎ{出|だ}す - to start swimming
・{飛|と}び{出|だ}す - to jump/rush out
・{笑|わら}い{出|だ}す - to start laughing
・{泣|な}き{出|だ}す - to start crying

USAGE NOTE:
{走|はし}り{出|だ}す focuses on the moment of starting to run, while {走|はし}り{出|で}る means to run out (of a place).
